embeds.title: 🔴 Iranian APT Nimbus Manticore Targets Aviation and Software Companies with Updated Tools
embeds.description:
**Actor:** Nimbus Manticore
Check Point reports that Iranian APT Nimbus Manticore (also known as Bohrium, Smoke Sandstorm, TA455, and UNC1549) has adopted new tactics and updated its arsenal in intrusions targeting aviation and software companies. The group, believed to be a subgroup of Charming Kitten (APT35) with ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, has shifted from DLL sideloading to AppDomain hijacking for payload execution. Recent campaigns targeted employees at aviation and software companies in Saudi Arabia and Australia with phishing lures distributing new backdoors including MiniJunk and MiniFast. The group also used fake job offers masquerading as US-based airlines and a fake SQL Developer download website. Check Point notes the group demonstrated capability likely supported by LLM-based tools and AI-assisted development techniques, with a shift towards targeting US-based organizations.
**Sources:** SecurityWeek • 🟡 2 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** Phishing with malicious attachments (ZIP archives, trojanized installers, fake software downloads)
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
